description: How to choose the oligomeric unit to cofold, for any enzyme. Separates two questions that are routinely conflated: (Q1) what oligomer does the protein form, and (Q2) does the LIGAND SITE require more than one subunit. Only Q2 determines what must be modeled. A homo-oligomer with N independent intra-subunit sites is correctly and far more cheaply modeled as a single subunit; an oligomer whose site straddles an interface must be modeled assembled. UniProt SUBUNIT answers Q1 only. This file holds the RULE; per-target measurements belong with the campaign that made them, not here.

decision_rule.statement: Model the ANNOTATED ASSEMBLY if and only if the catalytic site lies within the ligand's reach of a neighbouring subunit; otherwise model the FUNCTIONAL UNIT (the minimal unit carrying one complete active site).
decision_rule.rationale: The chemistry happens at the nucleophile, which is intra-subunit in essentially all hydrolase and transferase folds. What a neighbouring subunit can contribute is the SPECIFICITY CHANNEL accommodating the distal part of the substrate. The question is therefore geometric: can the substrate physically reach the interface from the catalytic centre.

interfacial_contact_fraction_threshold.meaning: fraction of ligand 5 A contact residues contributed by other chains, above which the site counts as interfacial

contact_radius_A.meaning: shell around a bound ligand used to define its contact residues

neighbourhood_radius_A.meaning: shell used to count nearby other-chain residues as a secondary descriptor

min_polymer_length.meaning: chains shorter than this are ignored as peptides/tags when mapping

min_ligand_heavy_atoms.meaning: a bound non-polymer component must have at least this many heavy atoms to be treated as substrate-like rather than an ion or small additive

ortholog_identity_threshold.meaning: Minimum pairwise sequence identity for one accession to inherit another's oligomeric verdict as an ortholog. Orthology is a much tighter relation than a shared domain: above this identity the subunit interface itself is typically conserved, so the donor's state transfers. Sits between own-annotation (rank 4) and shared-family transfer (rank 5).

transferable_interpro_types.meaning: Only a shared InterPro entry of these types licenses a family transfer. A shared homologous_superfamily or a bare signature/domain is far too broad - two enzymes can share an amidase signature or a C-N hydrolase superfamily domain while differing completely in oligomeric behaviour, so transferring an oligomeric verdict across one is unjustified.

ligand_reach.meaning: reach is measured from the reacting atom outward, since the distal end of the substrate is what reaches an interface; linear value is the sp3 chain extension per heavy atom

self_identity_threshold.meaning: At or above this sequence identity a deposited structure IS the query protein, not a relative. Evidence measured on it is direct (its own assembly, its own bound ligands) and must not be recorded as a transfer or discounted as one. Novel metagenomic and engineered sequences often have no UniProt accession while their structure is deposited, so identity to a PDB entry -- not the presence of an accession -- is what decides this.

non_substrate_het_codes._comment: Buffer, cryoprotectant and ion components. They bind crystal-packing interfaces and will manufacture a false interfacial signal if mistaken for substrate analogues. Extend as needed.

evidence_hierarchy.measurement: residues within contact_radius_A of a bound substrate/product/inhibitor, split by chain
evidence_hierarchy.note: The only direct, non-circular readout. Exclude non_substrate_het_codes.

evidence_hierarchy.measurement: are all catalytic residues (nucleophile, general base, oxyanion stabilisers, metal ligands) contributed by one chain?
evidence_hierarchy.strength: settles the chemistry, not the specificity channel

evidence_hierarchy.measurement: min distance from the catalytic nucleophile to any atom of another chain, in the LARGEST deposited biological assembly
evidence_hierarchy.interpretation: greater than ligand_reach => assembly cannot matter (strong negative); less than ligand_reach => assembly may matter (weak positive, does not establish that it does)

evidence_hierarchy.strength: answers Q1 only; never on its own a reason to cofold the oligomer

evidence_hierarchy.measurement: a liganded relative in the same InterPro family
evidence_hierarchy.strength: usable, must be recorded as transferred with the donor accession

guards.circularity: Evidence computed FROM poses docked into assembly X can never justify assembly X. Residues of a neighbouring chain can only appear near a ligand if that chain was placed there and the ligand had nowhere else to go. Breaking the circle requires an assembly-independent source: a deposited assembly, solution stoichiometry, or a liganded structure.
guards.control_first: Validate any site-interface probe on a case with a known answer BEFORE trusting it elsewhere. A probe returning 0% other-chain for a known interfacial site is measuring the wrong thing - e.g. a 5 A shell around a single nucleophile reports that residue's own buried environment, not the substrate channel.
guards.chain_counting: PDB assembly `oligomeric_count` counts CHAINS, not protomers. For a self-processing precursor deposited as one chain per protomer, `tetrameric(4)` means four protomers, not two. Misreading this inverts the conclusion.
guards.assembly_id: Assembly 1 is frequently the crystallographic monomer. Enumerate all assemblies and take the largest before concluding anything about oligomeric state.
guards.numbering: Map catalytic positions from UniProt numbering onto deposited chains by alignment; PDB author numbering routinely differs, and a silent mis-map produces a confident wrong answer.
guards.measure_from_the_nucleophile: An entry often annotates several active-site residues (nucleophile, proton donor, charge-relay). The distance test is only meaningful from the NUCLEOPHILE, where the scissile bond must sit; measuring from a proton donor moves the reference point several angstroms and can flip the verdict. Abstain rather than guess when no residue is annotated as the nucleophile.
guards.ambiguous_ligands: Small di/tri-carboxylates and polyols (e.g. malonate MLI, citrate CIT, tartrate TLA, succinate SIN) are both common crystallisation additives AND plausible substrate mimics for carboxylate-binding enzymes. A rank-1 verdict resting on one of these must be reported with its comp_id so a human can judge, not silently treated as a bound substrate.
guards.reach_is_an_upper_bound: ligand_reach assumes a fully extended ligand, so 'within reach' is permissive by construction and errs toward including subunits. It is therefore a strong NEGATIVE test (beyond reach => assembly cannot matter) and only a weak positive.

worked_examples._comment: Illustrations of the rule's two surprising outcomes, kept abstract - no campaign data.
worked_examples.annotated_oligomer_with_independent_site: A liganded homohexamer showing the same ligand bound in all six subunits with 0% other-chain contacts is modeled as ONE subunit; the hexamer costs ~36x more and adds nothing to the pocket.
worked_examples.small_oligomer_with_shared_site: A self-processing protomer whose nucleophile sits ~6-7 A from a neighbouring protomer across several independent crystals is modeled ASSEMBLED, even though its catalytic residues are all intra-chain.
